items.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 21 at 5:44AM AKST until November 22 at 3:00AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...South winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp, including Isabel
Pass.

* WHEN...Until 3 AM AKST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The peak of the winds for this event is
expected around noon Saturday.
items.areas: Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 21 at 5:42AM AKST until November 21 at 3:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow. Additional snow accumulations of 2 to 3 inches.

* WHERE...Dalton Highway Summits, South Slopes Of The Central Brooks
Range, and Upper Koyukuk Valley.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM AKST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The heaviest snowfall is expected along south
facing slopes, especially along the Brooks Range. Areas at lower
elevations, including along the Koyukuk River, are expected to see
lesser snow totals.
items.areas: South Slopes Of The Central Brooks Range; Upper Koyukuk Valley; Dalton Highway Summits
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit 511.alaska.gov or
call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 21 at 5:39AM AKST until November 21 at 3:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations of 4 to 8 inches.
Winds gusting as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...Central Brooks Range, primarily Atigun Pass.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM AKST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Near Atigun Pass periods of falling and
blowing snow could significantly reduce visibility to a half mile
or less at times. Snowfall will diminish Saturday morning.

items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 21 at 4:05AM AKST until November 23 at 3:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Elevated coastal water levels of 1 to 2 feet above the
normal highest tide line.

* WHERE...Coastal Kuskokwim Delta Communities, including Kipnuk,
Kongiganak, and Kwigillingok.

* WHEN...3 AM Sunday to 3 AM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Elevated coastal water levels driven by southeast
winds gusting to 55 mph. Coastal erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Gusty southeasterly winds will begin
increasing early Sunday morning as the storm approaches. Highest

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 20 at 3:15PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Confidence is growing in the potential for minor coastal erosion
and possible high surf conditions for parts of the West Coast as
a Bering Sea low passes by Monday and Tuesday. Primarily South to
Southeast wind directions could help water levels reach 1-3 feet
above the mean high tide level. No flooding is expected.
